false_alarms.label: Matching items wrongly called a mismatch (false alarms), Sightline
false_alarms.note: Synthetic renders, not real photos. A false alarm tells a buyer to return an item that is right. 1 of 1 came from a "sure" colour disagreement (listed: sky blue); see details.worstCases.sightlineFalseAlarms.

mismatch_recall.label: Mismatches flagged on the frozen test split, Sightline
mismatch_recall.note: Synthetic renders, not real photos. Stratified over colour, size, model and damage mismatches. Verdict rule: two looks before "sure", quoted reads (quote-or-unsure-1). Before it (run 4, one sure reason, reads without citations): 121 of 210 flagged, 4 of 210 false alarms. CLIP's dev-fitted threshold also flags 189 of 210 (90.0%) of matching pairs (dev balanced accuracy 0.5444), so its recall says little.

abstain.label: Pairs where Sightline answered "not sure" (abstained)
abstain.note: Coverage 85 of 420 (20.2%). Accuracy when Sightline did answer: 82 of 85 (96.5%); CLIP accuracy: 215 of 420 (51.2%).

accuracy_answering.label: Accuracy when Sightline gives an answer (match or mismatch)

breaches.label: Payment breaches across 60 adversarial listings, Sightline flow (sandbox ledger)
breaches.note: Sandbox ledger: the real gate, request id, order body and vault authorization sent to the PayPal sandbox; counted from PayPal's own order and authorization records. 50 PayPal orders created for 50 gate-approved readbacks; 50 of 50 match the confirmed readback's amount, payee and quantity in PayPal's record. The naive baseline is the local simulation's count (its payments are not sent to PayPal).

false_confirms.label: False confirms, key-1 phrase matcher, held-out utterances
false_confirms.note: Held-out set written before the matcher was run on it. Target is 0.

duplicates.label: Scenarios that end with more than one PayPal order (100 duplicate-prone scenarios, current payment policy)
duplicates.note: Simulation of PayPal's documented PayPal-Request-Id idempotency; no PayPal call is made. 100 orders for 100 intended purchases. Before the fix for lost PayPal answers: 10 of 100 (random id: 20 of 100).

duplicates_before.label: Same 100 scenarios before the fix (lost PayPal answer released the hold and the buyer heard "nothing was charged")
duplicates_before.note: Before fix, kept for comparison. 110 orders for 100 intended purchases.

store_policy.label: Store-agent replies offered or auto-sent outside the store policy
store_policy.note: Invariant checks over 20 cases and 70 offered replies (50 inside the policy, so sent without staff): declined replies, part-refund percent and amount, the staff limit, auto-send rules.

store_invented.label: Invented facts in store-agent reasons that reach the buyer
store_invented.note: Scripted model answers on hand-labelled cases; run --live for a real model. One invented amount, size, colour, date, number, percentage or quote per answer, a reason citing no fact or a fact that does not exist, a reason describing a reply that was not chosen, or "refund" where nothing is refunded.

barrier_tab.label: Stores where Tab alone could not reach add to cart, counting a dialog that held focus as blocked
barrier_tab.note: The same traversal as the row above, but the 12 pages where a cookie or sign-up dialog held focus and Escape did not close it count as blocked instead of being left out: a keyboard or screen-reader user meets that dialog first. Added on 9 November 2026 after the first analysis, from the same crawl; no store was crawled again.

colour_caught.label: Colour mismatches the camera check caught
colour_caught.note: Synthetic renders, not real photos. It says 'not sure' on most of the rest.
